summary: Modern databases have evolved beyond storage and querying to embed AI/ML capabilities natively, enabling vector search, LLM integration, and model inference directly within the data platform. By 2026, 75% of enterprise AI applications depend on vector search capabilities, and vector database adoption has grown 377% year over year, driving every major cloud data platform to ship first-class AI features. The result is a landscape where teams can run embeddings, semantic search, and generative AI workflows without moving data out of their primary database.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides a suite of serverless AI functions running natively in the Snowflake AI Data Cloud, including text-to-SQL (Cortex Analyst), document intelligence (Cortex Search), LLM inference via COMPLETE(), SUMMARIZE(), SENTIMENT(), TRANSLATE(), and EMBED_TEXT() for generating vector embeddings. Snowflake Postgres now runs natively in the platform and integrates pgvector for vector similarity search. Cortex AI also includes Cortex Fine-tuning for adapting LLMs on proprietary data, and Cortex Guard for safety filtering. All compute stays within Snowflakes governance boundary, so no data leaves the platform for inference.
databases.llm_integration: Native LLM inference via Cortex COMPLETE() supporting models such as Mistral, Llama 3, Reka, and Snowflake Arctic. Cortex Search delivers hybrid vector and keyword retrieval. Snowflake Postgres with pgvector extension adds vector similarity search natively. Text-to-SQL via Cortex Analyst connects natural language to structured data.
databases.pricing_notes: Cortex AI functions are billed in Snowflake credits. Embedding generation, LLM inference, and Cortex Search each consume credits at per-token or per-query rates that vary by model size. Cortex Search has a storage cost component plus query credits. Snowflake Postgres pricing follows standard Snowflake compute and storage rates. Exact per-token rates are published in the Snowflake service consumption table and vary by region.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML and Vertex AI Integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML allows data analysts to create and execute ML models using standard SQL, supporting logistic regression, boosted trees, matrix factorization, AutoML, and deep neural networks directly on BigQuery tables. BigQuery integrates with Vertex AI to enable remote model inference, embedding generation via the ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING function, and generative AI text tasks via ML.GENERATE_TEXT backed by Gemini models. BigQuery Vector Search (GA) enables approximate nearest neighbor search over embedding columns stored natively in BigQuery, supporting RAG pipelines without exporting data.
databases.llm_integration: Native integration with Google Gemini models (Gemini 1.5 Pro, Flash) via ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING SQL functions. Vertex AI Model Garden models can be called via remote functions. Supports embedding models including text-embedding-004 and multimodal embedding. LangChain and LlamaIndex connectors use BigQuery Vector Search as a retriever for RAG.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML model training and inference are billed per byte processed for SQL-based models. ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING calls are billed by tokens consumed on the underlying Vertex AI or Gemini model, plus standard BigQuery query costs. BigQuery Vector Search queries are billed at standard on-demand query pricing per byte scanned. Flat-rate and BigQuery editions (Standard, Enterprise, Enterprise Plus) can cover ML compute under reserved slots.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.description: pgvector is an open-source PostgreSQL extension that adds vector data types and similarity search operators, supporting exact and approximate nearest neighbor search via HNSW and IVFFlat indexes. It is the lowest-friction path to vector search for teams already running Postgres, requiring no new infrastructure, preserving existing security models and backup procedures, and handling up to 50 million vectors comfortably in production. pgai, developed by Timescale, extends Postgres further to call LLM APIs (OpenAI, Ollama, Cohere, Anthropic) directly from SQL, generate embeddings automatically via triggers, and run semantic search queries in standard SQL. Together they enable full RAG pipelines inside Postgres.
databases.llm_integration: pgai enables direct SQL calls to OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, and Cohere APIs from within Postgres functions and triggers. Embedding generation can be automated on insert or update. pgvector integrates with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and Django as a vector store backend. Snowflake Postgres and Supabase both ship pgvector as a managed extension, broadening its reach into cloud-managed environments.
databases.pricing_notes: pgvector and pgai are open-source and free to use on self-hosted Postgres. Managed offerings include Supabase (free tier available, pro from $25/month), Timescale Cloud (usage-based), AWS RDS for PostgreSQL (standard RDS instance pricing plus storage), Google Cloud SQL, and Azure Database for PostgreSQL. LLM API calls made through pgai are billed by the respective LLM provider at their standard token rates.

databases.name: Amazon (Aurora ML + Redshift ML)
databases.ai_feature: Aurora ML, Redshift ML, and pgvector on Aurora PostgreSQL
databases.description: Amazon Aurora ML integrates Aurora (MySQL and PostgreSQL-compatible) with Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Comprehend, allowing SQL-based invocation of ML models for inference without moving data out of the database. Aurora PostgreSQL supports the pgvector extension for vector similarity search, enabling RAG workloads natively. Redshift ML uses CREATE MODEL SQL syntax backed by Amazon SageMaker Autopilot to train classification, regression, and forecasting models on Redshift data, with results queryable as SQL functions. Amazon Bedrock integration allows Redshift and Aurora to call foundation models including Titan Embeddings and Anthropic Claude via SQL-level functions.
databases.llm_integration: Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector supports vector storage and ANN search with HNSW and IVFFlat indexes. Aurora ML invokes SageMaker endpoints and Amazon Comprehend (sentiment, entity detection) via SQL functions. Redshift ML calls SageMaker Autopilot for automated model training and exposes predictions as SQL functions. Amazon Bedrock integration (in preview and GA across services) enables Titan Embeddings generation and Claude-based text inference callable from database contexts via Lambda or direct connector.
databases.pricing_notes: Aurora ML inference calls are billed per SageMaker endpoint invocation or Comprehend API call at standard AWS service rates, on top of Aurora instance and storage costs. pgvector on Aurora PostgreSQL has no additional licensing cost beyond the Aurora instance. Redshift ML model training via SageMaker Autopilot incurs SageMaker training job costs. Redshift ML inference uses Redshift compute (billed under existing cluster or Serverless pricing). Bedrock API calls are billed per token by model.

databases.name: Databricks (MLflow + DBRX)
databases.ai_feature: Databricks AI — MLflow, DBRX, Mosaic AI, and Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks provides an end-to-end AI platform combining MLflow for experiment tracking, model registry, and deployment; Mosaic AI for fine-tuning and serving LLMs; DBRX as Databricks' own open-source high-quality LLM; and Databricks Vector Search for managed ANN retrieval over Delta Lake tables. Vector Search creates indexes directly on Delta tables and keeps them automatically synchronized as data updates, eliminating a separate vector database. Unity Catalog governs all ML models and vector indexes with the same access controls applied to data. Databricks also integrates with pgvector environments for teams mirroring Postgres data into the Lakehouse.
databases.llm_integration: Databricks Model Serving hosts DBRX, Llama 3, Mixtral, and external models behind a unified inference API. Foundation Model APIs provide pay-per-token access to curated LLMs without managing infrastructure. MLflow AI Gateway proxies calls to OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, and other providers with rate limiting and credential management. LangChain and LlamaIndex have native Databricks Vector Search integrations. Retrieval-augmented generation chains can be built entirely within a Databricks notebook using Vector Search as the retriever and Model Serving as the generator.
databases.pricing_notes: Databricks billing is in DBUs (Databricks Units). Vector Search index creation and synchronization consume DBUs based on compute used. Model Serving (for DBRX and other hosted models) is billed per token or per provisioned throughput tier. Foundation Model API usage is billed per token at published rates. MLflow tracking and registry are included in the Databricks workspace at no extra charge. Databricks SQL and Jobs compute used for ML pipelines follow standard DBU pricing per workload type.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search enables storing, indexing, and querying high-dimensional vector embeddings alongside operational document data in the same MongoDB collection, eliminating the need for a separate vector store. It uses an HNSW index (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) for approximate nearest neighbor search and supports pre-filtering on any document field to combine metadata filtering with semantic similarity in a single query. Atlas Vector Search integrates with LangChain, LlamaIndex, Hugging Face, and Amazon Bedrock to support full RAG pipelines. It is available on all Atlas tiers including the free M0 cluster with a vector index limit, and scales to multi-billion vector workloads on dedicated clusters.
databases.llm_integration: Atlas Vector Search connects natively to LangChain and LlamaIndex as a vector store retriever. Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases supports Atlas as a managed vector store backend. Integration with OpenAI, Cohere, Hugging Face, and Google Vertex AI embedding models is handled at the application layer via official connectors. MongoDB Atlas also offers Atlas Stream Processing and aggregation pipelines that can invoke external AI APIs, and the Atlas Data API enables serverless access from AI agent frameworks.
databases.pricing_notes: Atlas Vector Search is included in all Atlas clusters at no separate feature charge. Costs are based on the underlying Atlas cluster tier (M0 free, M10 from approximately $0.08/hour, M30 and above for production vector workloads). Vector index storage counts toward Atlas storage consumption. Serverless Atlas instances support vector search with usage-based pricing per read and write unit. Higher throughput and billion-scale vector workloads require dedicated M40 or larger clusters with corresponding instance pricing.
